case_name: Arun Kumar Agarwal vs Radha Arun And Anr.

parties.respondent_defendant: Radha Arun and another (wife and alleged adulterer)

facts_of_case: The husband filed a petition under Section 13(1)(i) of the Hindu Marriage Act, alleging adultery. The trial court allowed the petition.

legal_principles.principle: A person impleaded as a co-respondent in a petition under Section 13(1)(i) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, as alleged adulterer, cannot seek deletion on the ground that no relief is sought against him.
legal_principles.held: Once the petitioner chooses to implead as a co-respondent, the person who according to him is the adulterer, he being a proper party, cannot be deleted at the instance of such respondent.

legal_principles.principle: An adulterer is a proper, if not necessary party to a proceedings under Section 13(1)(i) of the Hindu Marriage Act.
legal_principles.held: The principles relating to impleading of parties make it clear that an adulterer is a proper, if not necessary party to a proceedings under Section 13(1)(i) of the Hindu Marriage Act.

outcome.final_order: The alleged adulterer is a proper party to the proceedings and cannot seek deletion from the petition.

use_for_drafting: representing clients in Hindu Marriage Act cases
